newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG offers aid cut to help Radio Australia.
newsitem.headline: PNG offers aid cut to help Radio Australia.

text.p: The South Pacific nation of Papua New Guinea volunteered on Wednesday to take a one million kina (US$720,000) cut in Australian aid to help save threatened overseas radio service Radio Australia.

Papua New Guinea (PNG) Prime Minister Julius Chan told the Australian High Commissioner in the capital Port Moresby that his nation would be left considerably worse off by the closure of Radio Australia. He said the network had an estimated weekly audience of 4.9 million in Asia and the Pacific.
"Papua New Guinea as a developing nation and regional focal point has come to depend on Radio Australia as representative of excellency in broadcasting," Chan said in a letter.
A recent inquiry into budget cuts at Australia's national broadcaster, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation, recommended the closure of Radio Australia to save A$25 million (US$19 million) a year.
The proposal has sparked a campaign to save the short-wave service, which has been operating since 1939.
Local media reports this week said Australia's diplomatic service had argued against closure, saying Radio Australia played a valuable role in advancing the country's interests.
Chan said in a statement that the one million kina could be deducted from the current Australian aid budget to PNG over the next five years.
